leaders.notes: Marian's 6th (some sources: 7th) president, 1989-1999; left to become president of Capital University in Ohio. A successor served roughly 1999-2001 before Elsener's appointment, but that person's identity could not be confirmed in available public sources despite multiple searches -- likely a short interim/acting presidency; flagged as a research gap rather than fabricated.

Became Marian's 8th president on August 1, 2001, and remains the sitting president as of 2025 (24+ years, one of the longest-serving college presidents in Indiana). Earlier career included teacher, high school principal, superintendent of Catholic Schools for the Diocese of Wichita, and head of Catholic education for the Archdiocese of Indianapolis. Note: an unrelated, same-named 'Marian University' in Fond du Lac, Wisconsin has its own separate and much more frequently turned-over president list (Ridenour, DiSalvo, Fale, Manion, Majewski, etc.); care was taken not to conflate the two institutions.
9th president; longest presidential tenure at Mary Baldwin since it became a four-year college in 1923. Announced retirement in 2022, stepped down in June 2023.

leaders.nextRole: Chief Integration Officer and Executive Vice President
leaders.notes: 10th president and the first male president of Mary Baldwin since 1976. Inaugurated October 2024; abruptly resigned in August 2025, about two years into the job, reportedly for personal reasons. His departure prompted a faculty 'no confidence' vote against the Board of Trustees over how it was handled. He returned to his prior employer, Elon University, in a senior role by the end of 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President and Dean, Murphy Deming College of Health Sciences
leaders.notes: 11th president; confirmed effective immediately upon Stein's sudden August 2025 resignation, promoted from within after serving as VP/Dean of MBU's health sciences college since 2023.

Succeeded longtime president Sister Marie Majella Berg (1960-1993) as Marymount's 4th president; last of Marymount's Religious of the Sacred Heart of Mary (RSHM) presidents before the school moved to lay leadership.
5th president and Marymount's first lay (non-religious) president; served 10 years, announcing retirement effective June 30, 2011.

6th president; announced in late 2017 he would step down at the end of the 2017-18 academic year (effective June 30, 2018). Later became president of the Virginia Foundation for Independent Colleges (Jan. 2019) and was named Marymount president emeritus.
7th president and Marymount's first Latina president, took office July 1, 2018; previously spent 16 years at Florida International University before St. Thomas University. Still serving as of 2026.

Led Maryville for roughly 12-13 years, overseeing significant 1990s campus construction (Art & Design Building). Announced retirement in Sept. 2004, effective at the end of the 2004-05 academic year; Maryville's Keith Lovin Institute for Leadership and Values is named for him. Start/end years are approximate, reconstructed from a 2004 news article describing his tenure length; a successor was not in place until Mark Lombardi arrived in 2007, suggesting an approximately two-year acting/interim leadership gap (2005-2007) whose occupant could not be identified in available public sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost / Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 10th president; served 18 years, one of the longest tenures of any sitting university president nationally by the time he retired in 2025. Led major digital-learning and enrollment-growth initiatives.

11th president, effective June 2025, succeeding the retiring Mark Lombardi. Previously president of Pittsburg State University (since 2022) and before that a vice chancellor at the University of Nebraska Medical Center and University of Nebraska Omaha.
